historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.1% vs revenue 9.3% (46% divergence): equity lags because ~40-46% of core profit is paid out as dividends and FY2024 carried a ¥40bn buyback, not because of earnings quality. The base path uses management guidance and the dated exclusivity cliffs, not either CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (reported FCF less SBC less interest income; SBC only disclosed FY2021-25, taken as 0 before) are not meaningful for this company: FCF is dominated by lumpy in-licensing cash (FY2024 ¥79bn, FY2025 ¥46bn intangibles) and FY2025 cash tax was a net refund. FY2025 owner FCF ¥7.5bn vs FY2022 ¥15.8bn vs FY2020 ¥2.5bn. Revenue 10yr CAGR is only 3.2% (FY2015 ¥364bn) because the Kyowa Hakko Bio business was deconsolidated in FY2018 and the APAC business restructured in FY2025; the underlying global-strategic-product franchise (Crysvita + Poteligeo, ~52% of revenue) has compounded well above 10%. FY2025 revenue (+0.3%) is not a cyclical peak: it absorbed APAC restructuring and a -9% Japan year while North America grew +10%; H1 FY2026 is +14.3%.

scenario_narratives.base: Franchise strength through FY2027 (Crysvita/Poteligeo double-digit, KOMZIFTI launch, FY2026 core OP guidance already raised once to ¥130bn), then the three dated headwinds management itself names: Fasenra royalty end 2028, Poteligeo exclusivity 2030, Crysvita exclusivity 2032. Revenue peaks ~¥590bn in FY2030-31, dips ~6% over FY2032-33 and stabilises as the pipeline (KOMZIFTI label expansion, Lenmeldy, KK8123, infigratinib, OTL-203) partially refills; owner EBITDA margin rebuilds from the FY2028 R&D-step-up trough to 27% (core OP ~25%, a haircut to the 30% target). Capex stays above D&A to fund the Sanford plant and ~3%/yr of in-licensing. Net cash ¥265bn is added at face; the equity-method and financial-asset book (¥25bn) at book.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vision 2030 delivered: ~10% revenue CAGR to 2030 driven by Crysvita geographic/indication expansion, Poteligeo, KOMZIFTI frontline AML combinations and Lenmeldy newborn-screening demand; margin reaches the 30% core OP target (32% owner EBITDA) as R&D intensity normalises; exclusivity expiries slow growth to 2-3% in FY2032-33 but do not shrink the business. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Guidance met in FY2026, then US MFN pricing and faster-than-expected biosimilar erosion of both franchise antibodies, continued -9%/yr Japan decline, Fasenra royalty loss, and a thin post-rocatinlimab pipeline that fails to replace them. Revenue down ~30% from peak by FY2034, owner EBITDA margin to 15%, in-licensing spend up. Net cash cushions the equity value; the operating business is worth well under today's EV.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A net-cash, ~¥500bn-revenue specialty pharma valued on owner FCF built from the company's own core operating profit, with the cash part of 'non-recurring' charges treated as recurring, in-licensing charged through capex (and impairments therefore not double-charged), leases charged in the flows and excluded from net debt, interest income stripped against the ¥265bn cash pile, and the three management-dated exclusivity/royalty cliffs modelled explicitly inside a 10-year horizon. The ten-year base revenue CAGR is 1.7% against management's 10% ambition; the bull case is management's plan, the bear is a franchise cliff without a pipeline. JPY WACC 7.5% across all scenarios; terminal value capped at 18x FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Crysvita exclusivity expiry (2032) and Poteligeo (2030): the base assumes slow antibody-style erosion (-3%/yr group revenue for two years); a US biosimilar entering at launch would push the base toward the bear path
US Most-Favored-Nation drug pricing: ~39% of revenue is North American; a 20-30% US price cut on the franchise is not in the base

Pipeline execution post-rocatinlimab: KOMZIFTI (50:50 with Kura), Lenmeldy, KK8123, infigratinib, OTL-203 must deliver roughly ¥100bn of replacement revenue by the mid-2030s for the base's flat-to-+2% post-cliff path
Margin trough in FY2028 (Fasenra royalty end plus R&D step-up) could be deeper or longer than the 24.5% modelled
FX: ~74% of revenue in USD/GBP/EUR reported in JPY; a 10% yen appreciation is roughly -7% on revenue and more on core OP
Capital allocation of the ¥265bn net cash (added at face): Kirin Holdings' ~50% stake means buybacks are episodic (¥40bn FY2024, ¥9m FY2025); value-destroying M&A would erode the bridge
In-licensing cash normalised at ~3% of revenue; a Kura-sized upfront every two years would run nearer 5%

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Securities Report, consolidated cash flow statement share-based payment expense (¥857m); restricted-share and performance-linked share remuneration to directors only. Equity-award cash taxes: none disclosed (0).
inputs.share_count_basis: 525,634,500 issued less 2,048,889 treasury = 523,585,611 at 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 tanshin). No potential shares (diluted EPS not stated because none exist). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. buyback_cash is FY2025 actual (¥9m); FY2024 was ¥40.0bn, so the count is funded only episodically.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T06:30:00Z (TSE regular close, Friday 30 Oct; Yahoo chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built: 10y JGB ~1.7% + 6.0% ERP x beta ~0.95 (Japanese pharma, but ~74% of revenue in USD/GBP/EUR adds FX volatility to JPY flows) = ~7.4%; rounded to 7.5%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same rate across all three scenarios; risk lives in the flows (scenario paths and weights), not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Lease principal (¥5,983m FY2025, financing CF) plus lease interest (¥838m, IFRS 16 note) = ¥6,821m = 1.37% of revenue charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (1.3%). Lease liabilities (¥26,130m at 2025-12-31; the ENTIRE 'interest-bearing debt' line - there are no bank borrowings or bonds) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: total_debt = 0. D&A for the cash-tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation (¥4,297m FY2025) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: total equity equals equity attributable to owners (¥916,165m both) - Kirin Holdings' ~50% stake is at the listco level, not an NCI inside it.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating pharma; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md, owner-fcf.md + adaptations (a1 JPY WACC, b leases, d matching asset, e near-SBC-zero)). First valuation of this ticker. EBITDA margin is anchored on the company's NEW core operating profit (FY2025 ¥109.8bn, 22.1%; FY2026 guidance ¥130.0bn on ¥520.0bn, 25.0%, raised from ¥100bn in May 2026 and reaffirmed in Aug 2026) plus depreciation ex sales-rights amortisation (~¥18bn), LESS a recurring 2% of revenue for the cash portion of 'non-recurring' charges that this company books every year (restructuring, collaboration losses, deal costs; FY2021-25 PBT ran ¥5-24bn below core OP annually). Non-cash impairments of in-licensed intangibles are NOT charged in EBITDA because the in-licensing cash is already charged through capex (FY2024 ¥79.2bn intangibles incl. Orchard-related, FY2025 ¥45.8bn Kura/ziftomenib upfront) - charging both would double count. Capex path (PPE + intangibles) normalises in-licensing at ~3% of revenue (FY2019-23 average ¥16bn) on top of PPE (Sanford NC plant build keeps PPE at ~7% through FY2027, then ~4-4.5%). last_fcf (FY2025 owner FCF ¥7.5bn) is NOT a run-rate: it carries the ¥45.8bn Kura upfront and a ¥0.2bn net tax REFUND; the component build, not last_fcf, drives the projections. Cash tax ramps 24% -> 28% (blended Japan ~30.6% / US / UK; FY2024 cash tax 21% of PBT, FY2026 guidance implies ~21% with closing-cost deductions). Interest income (¥4,711m FY2025) stripped because net cash ¥265bn >> FCF base; the matching asset is the cash in net_debt. Equity-method investments and other financial assets (whose income sits outside core OP) added in equity_bridge at book. Horizon 10 years (FY2026-FY2035) because management's own dated cliffs - Fasenra royalty end 2028, Poteligeo exclusivity 2030, Crysvita 2032 - fall inside it; the base revenue path carries them explicitly rather than hiding them in terminal growth. SBC is 0.17% of revenue: house and street bases nearly coincide; band_position is close to degenerate and should be read as n/a.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance, then US MFN pricing clips Crysvita/Poteligeo from FY2028, the Fasenra royalty ends, Poteligeo (2030) and Crysvita (2032) erode faster than an antibody franchise normally would, the Japan legacy book keeps shrinking 8-9%/yr, and the post-rocatinlimab pipeline (KOMZIFTI 50:50 with Kura, Lenmeldy, KK8123, infigratinib) is too small to refill. Revenue falls ~30% from the FY2027 peak; margins compress to 15% as fixed R&D and the new plants are spread over a smaller base; in-licensing spend rises to buy replacements.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +7% (guidance ¥520bn = +4.7% is conservative against H1 +14.3%); FY2027 +6%; FY2028 +4% as the Fasenra royalty ends; FY2029-30 +3%/+1% with Poteligeo exclusivity expiring 2030; FY2032-33 -3%/-3% for Crysvita exclusivity expiry (antibody for an ultra-rare disease: slow, partial biosimilar erosion, not a small-molecule cliff); FY2034-35 flat/+2% as KOMZIFTI, Lenmeldy, KK8123, infigratinib and OTL-203 partially refill. Ten-year revenue CAGR 1.7% vs management's 10% ambition.
base.margin_note: Owner EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-lease) = new core OP + depreciation ex sales-rights amortisation - 2% recurring cash non-core. FY2026 24.8%: core OP 25% guided + ~3.8% depreciation - 2% recurring - ~2% rocatinlimab closing costs (¥10.4bn provisions booked H1 FY2026, one-off). FY2027 27% as closing costs lapse. FY2028 24.5%: management's own 'low 20% range' core OP margin year (Fasenra royalty gone, R&D step-up). Then rebuild to 27% (core OP ~25%) by FY2035 - a haircut to the 30% Vision 2030 target, held through the Crysvita expiry.
base.capex_note: PPE ~7% (Sanford NC plant, Takasaki) FY2026-27 easing to ~4.5%, plus normalised in-licensing ~3% of revenue; FY2024-25 lumpy upfronts (Orchard, Kura) are the kind of outlay the 3% averages. Capex exceeds D&A at terminal by ~2.5% of revenue - that is the cost of replacing a franchise with dated exclusivity.
base.tax_note: FY2025 cash tax was a ¥204m net refund (prepayment timing); FY2024 cash tax 21% of PBT; H1 FY2026 accrual ~30%. Ramp 24% -> 28% blended statutory.

bull.narrative: Management's Vision 2030 delivered: ~10% revenue CAGR to 2030 and a 30% core OP margin (32% owner EBITDA) by the early 2030s; the exclusivity expiries dent growth (FY2032-33 +3%/+2%) but KOMZIFTI, Lenmeldy (RUSP newborn screening) and the FGF23/achondroplasia pipeline more than refill.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: ~52% of revenue sits in two antibodies with management-dated exclusivity expiries (2030/2032), the most advanced non-franchise asset (rocatinlimab) was discontinued in March 2026 on a safety signal, and North America (~39% of revenue) is directly exposed to MFN pricing. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs KOMZIFTI, Lenmeldy and at least one of KK8123/infigratinib/OTL-203 to succeed together to offset the cliffs. Base 50%: the base path already carries the dated cliffs explicitly, so the weights price pipeline execution, not the cliffs twice.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
